use: Signals you're about to leave a visit, a cafe or a party; the 'go home' part is left unsaid.

example.ja: じゃあそろそろ。明日早いし。
example.english: Well, I should go. I've got an early start.

examplePolite.romaji: Dewa sorosoro shitsurei shimasu. Gochisousama deshita.
examplePolite.ja: ではそろそろ失礼します。ごちそうさまでした。
examplePolite.english: Well, I'll be going. Thank you for the meal.

politeJa: そろそろ行きましょうか
use: Suggests to the group that it's time to leave, or to move on to the next place.

example.romaji: Mou juuji da. Sorosoro ikou ka.
example.ja: もう十時だ。そろそろ行こうか。
example.english: It's already ten. Shall we get going?

examplePolite.romaji: Mou juuji desu ne. Sorosoro ikimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: もう十時ですね。そろそろ行きましょうか。
examplePolite.english: It's already ten. Shall we get going?

notes: Swap the verb: sorosoro kaerou ka (shall we head home?).

english: I'm heading off (before you); after you
use: Short form for leaving before others, or with douzo for letting someone go first.

example.english: Okay, I'm heading off! Good work.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、お先に失礼します。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I'll be leaving before you.

notes: Also before eating or bathing first: osaki ni itadakimasu.

kana: おさきにしつれいします
english: I'll be leaving now, before you
use: Said to coworkers still working when you leave; they answer otsukaresama deshita.

example.romaji: Kyou wa kore de, osaki ni shitsurei shimasu.
example.ja: 今日はこれで、お先に失礼します。
example.english: That's it for me today. I'll head off before you.

notes: Also for leaving a party or meeting early.

kana: きをつけてかえってね
politeJa: 気をつけてお帰りください
use: Said to someone heading home, especially at night or in bad weather; answer un, arigatou.

example.romaji: Mou kurai kara, ki o tsukete kaette ne.
example.ja: もう暗いから、気をつけて帰ってね。
example.english: It's dark now, so get home safe.

examplePolite.romaji: Ame ga tsuyoi node, ki o tsukete okaeri kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 雨が強いので、気をつけてお帰りください。
examplePolite.english: It's raining hard, so get home safely.

notes: Ki o tsukete alone means take care, or watch out.

use: Polite send-off to someone leaving: a guest, a customer, a coworker going on a trip.

example.romaji: Kyou wa arigatou gozaimashita. Oki o tsukete.
example.ja: 今日はありがとうございました。お気をつけて。
example.english: Thank you for today. Take care.

use: Said when you won't see someone for a long time, like before a move or at the end of a trip.

example.romaji: Mukou de mo genki de ne.
example.english: Take care of yourself over there.

examplePolite.romaji: Atarashii shigoto, ganbatte kudasai. Ogenki de.
examplePolite.ja: 新しい仕事、頑張ってください。お元気で。
examplePolite.english: Good luck with the new job. Take care.

notes: Not for an ordinary daily goodbye; it implies a long time apart.

politeJa: よろしくお伝えください
english: say hi to them for me
use: Sends your regards to someone who isn't there, usually as you part: X ni yoroshiku tsutaete.

example.ja: お母さんによろしく伝えてね。
example.english: Say hi to your mom for me.

examplePolite.ja: 奥さんによろしくお伝えください。
examplePolite.english: Please give my regards to your wife.

notes: Often cut to just X ni yoroshiku.

use: The default summer opener with neighbours, shop staff or coworkers; agree with hontou ni, atsui desu ne.

example.romaji: Kyou mo atsui desu ne. Ase ga tomaranai desu.
example.ja: 今日も暑いですね。汗が止まらないです。
example.english: Hot again today, isn't it? I can't stop sweating.

notes: With friends: atsui ne. Hot food and baths are atsui too.

use: The winter version of atsui desu ne; an easy way to greet anyone.

example.romaji: Kesa wa hontou ni samui desu ne.
example.ja: 今朝は本当に寒いですね。
example.english: It's really cold this morning, isn't it?

notes: With friends: samui ne. For cold drinks or water, use tsumetai, not samui.

use: Light opener with a neighbour or someone at a bus stop; agree with sou desu ne.

example.romaji: Kyou wa ii tenki desu ne. Osanpo desu ka?
example.ja: 今日はいい天気ですね。お散歩ですか？
example.english: Lovely day today. Out for a walk?

notes: With friends: ii tenki da ne.

use: A neighbour's greeting when they see you leaving; it isn't really asking where, so answer vaguely.

example.romaji: A, ohayou gozaimasu. Odekake desu ka?
example.ja: あ、おはようございます。お出かけですか？

notes: The stock answer is ee, chotto soko made (just up the road).

english: that really helped; you saved me
use: Thanks that stresses the relief someone gave you, like lending you something or covering for you.

example.romaji: Kasa kashite kurete, hontou ni tasukatta yo.
example.ja: 傘貸してくれて、本当に助かったよ。
example.english: Thanks for lending me the umbrella, it really saved me.

examplePolite.romaji: Kasa o kashite kudasatte, hontou ni tasukarimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 傘を貸してくださって、本当に助かりました。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for lending me the umbrella, it really helped.

notes: Also 'phew, saved' after a close call. Tasukaru (present) accepts an offer: sou shite kureru to tasukaru.

politeJa: いろいろありがとうございました
use: Thanks for help over a stretch of time, often when someone leaves or a trip ends.

example.ja: この一週間、いろいろありがとうね。

examplePolite.ja: この一週間、いろいろありがとうございました。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for everything this week.

src: いつもありがとうございます
ja: いつもありがとうございます
kana: いつもありがとうございます
use: Thanks for continuing help: staff to regular customers, or you to a coworker or delivery driver you see often.

example.romaji: Itsumo arigatou gozaimasu. Kyou wa nan ni shimasu ka?
example.ja: いつもありがとうございます。今日は何にしますか？
example.english: Thanks for coming again. What'll it be today?

notes: To family or friends: itsumo arigatou ne.

english: thank you for all your help (at the end)
use: Said when a stay, job or course of care ends: to a host family, your old boss, hospital staff.

example.romaji: Sannenkan, hontou ni osewa ni narimashita.
example.ja: 三年間、本当にお世話になりました。
example.english: Thank you so much for these three years.

notes: The ongoing form, osewa ni natte imasu, opens work emails and calls.
